answer: A registry issues each agent one identity bonded to a stake and a trail of work. Attestation is sampled: peers must vouch, and those peers hold aged bonds, so fresh keys cannot certify themselves. A clone caught faking history forfeits its bond and attestation rights. A meadow of new accounts buys nothing until it pays for real verification: stake per key, fees per round, elapsed time. Like light through a prism, each record splits into one line of provenance. An honest operator reads the atlas once; a forger must rebuild it for every key, paying linearly where honest work pays once.
